videos.title: 学习如何学习
videos.original_title: Learning how to learn | Barbara Oakley | TEDxOaklandUniversity
videos.creator: Barbara Oakley

chapters.title: 从数学掉队到工程教授：探索有效学习的缘起
chapters.summary: 讲者回顾自己因频繁搬家而在数学学习上掉队，随后参军学习俄语、担任翻译并前往南极的经历。接触工程师的解题方式后，她在26岁退伍时决定重新学习数理知识。为理解这一转变，她向擅长教学的教授请教，并研究神经科学与认知心理学，引出有效学习的主题。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker introduces her search for effective learning methods through her personal history. Frequent moves disrupted her sequential math education, and she struggled with math and science before eventually becoming an engineering professor. She recounts joining the army to learn Russian, working as a translator on Soviet trawlers in the Bering Sea, and visiting Antarctica, where she met her husband. Exposure to West Point engineers and their problem-solving abilities inspired her to pursue math, science, and technology after leaving the military at age 26. To understand how she made this transition, she consulted professors who taught effectively, noticed similarities in their learning and teaching practices, and investigated neuroscience and cognitive psychology. This unit introduces the motivation for the talk without yet presenting the specific learning techniques.

points.title: 频繁搬家、数学掉队与成为工程教授的反差
参军学俄语、担任翻译与南极经历
接触工程师的解题方式，萌生学习数理知识的愿望
26岁退伍后决定改变自己的学习方向
请教教授并研究认知科学，寻找有效学习的方法

chapters.title: 专注与发散模式：通过切换思维突破学习卡点
chapters.summary: 用弹球机比喻解释两种思维模式：专注模式沿熟悉路径深入思考，发散模式让思路更广，有助于接近新概念。学习或解题卡住时，可暂时转移注意力，让发散模式在后台发挥作用，再回到专注模式加工想法。达利握钥匙放松、爱迪生据传握滚珠小憩的例子，说明如何在两种模式间切换；解决对自己而言的新问题也是创造性活动。
chapters.english_summary: Explains focused and diffuse modes of thinking through a pinball-machine analogy. Focused thinking follows familiar pathways, such as historical patterns or multiplication tables, while diffuse thinking ranges more widely and helps approach unfamiliar concepts. The speaker recommends alternating between the modes and shifting attention away when stuck so resting states can work in the background. Salvador Dali's practice of relaxing with keys in his hand illustrates returning from diffuse ideas to focused refinement when falling keys wake him. A similar story about Thomas Edison holding ball bearings is explicitly presented as a legend. The unit concludes that solving a problem or exploring an idea that is new to the learner is a creative activity, even if others have solved it before.

points.title: 认识专注模式与放松的发散模式
弹球机比喻：熟悉路径与探索新思路
学习卡住时转移注意力，让发散模式发挥作用
达利握钥匙放松：醒来后专注加工绘画灵感
爱迪生握滚珠的传说：切换模式完善发明及对学习的启示

chapters.title: 用番茄工作法应对拖延：专注25分钟，再短暂放松
chapters.summary: 讲者解释，面对不想做的任务时，人可能感到痛苦；继续投入几分钟，这种感觉会消退，而转移注意力虽能立即缓解不适，反复如此却可能形成类似成瘾的模式。番茄工作法要求关闭干扰、计时专注25分钟，随后短暂放松，同时练习专注与休息。关键是承诺专注一段时间，而非要求自己在这段时间内完成全部作业。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker explains procrastination as a response to discomfort when facing an unwanted task. Continuing to work can allow that discomfort to fade within a few minutes, while turning attention away provides immediate relief and, when repeated frequently, can become addiction-like. The speaker introduces the Pomodoro Technique: use any timer, set it for 25 minutes, turn off distractions such as instant messaging, and work with focused attention. Follow the session with a few minutes of enjoyable relaxation. This practices both focus and relaxation, with relaxation also described as part of learning. The key is to commit to 25 minutes of focused work rather than demand completion of an entire homework set within that time.

points.title: 拖延的起点：面对不想做的任务时感到痛苦
继续投入或转移注意力：两种应对及其后果
番茄工作法：关闭干扰，计时专注25分钟
专注后短暂放松，练习专注与休息
关键是专注25分钟，而非完成整份作业

chapters.title: 重新看待学习中的“弱点”：创造力与慢思考的优势
chapters.summary: 讲者指出，学生眼中的弱点也可能带来优势：工作记忆较弱或注意力容易转移，可能让其他想法进入，从而促进创造力；思考较慢则如徒步者相对于赛车手，虽需更多努力理解材料，却可能获得更深入的体验，避免仓促下结论，并扎实掌握所学。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker reframes perceived learning weaknesses as possible strengths. Poor working memory and a tendency for attention to drift can allow other ideas to enter, which the speaker links to greater creativity. Slow thinking is compared to hiking rather than race car driving: although slower thinkers may need to work harder to understand the material, they can notice more, develop deeper understanding, avoid jumping to conclusions, and gain solid mastery.

points.title: 学生可能把自身优势误认为弱点
工作记忆较弱：其他想法进入可能带来创造力
注意力容易转移也可能带来新想法
慢思考的优势：用徒步者与赛车手作比喻
慢思考虽需更多努力，却可能换来扎实掌握

chapters.title: 学习中的能力错觉与考试焦虑
chapters.summary: 学习一整天也可能因方法无效而徒劳。许多情况下，考试焦虑源于突然发现自己并未真正掌握所学内容。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces illusions of competence in learning: studying all day can produce little progress when study techniques are ineffective. It then explains that, in many cases, test anxiety arises from confronting the frightening realization that one has not mastered the material.

points.title: 能力错觉：学习时间长不代表方法有效
考试焦虑可能源于发现自己尚未掌握知识

chapters.title: 运动有助于提升学习与记忆能力
chapters.summary: 对动物和人类的研究发现，运动可在短短几天内提高学习与记忆能力，研究人员也正逐步理解其背后的神经生理机制。
chapters.english_summary: Research involving animals and people identifies exercise as a way to improve learning and memory within a few days. Researchers are beginning to understand the neurophysiological pathways behind these effects.

points.title: 运动可在几天内提高学习与记忆能力
研究逐步揭示背后的神经生理机制

chapters.title: 用自测、主动回忆与重复练习巩固学习
chapters.summary: 通过小测验、打乱顺序的闪卡和跨多天重做作业题巩固学习；以唱歌不能只唱一次就学会为例，说明反复练习的必要性。阅读后移开视线并回忆，比单纯划重点或重读更有效。理解还需结合不同情境下的练习与重复，才能达到熟练掌握。结尾鼓励学会学习，并拓展自己的兴趣。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker recommends frequent mini-tests, shuffled flashcards even for math and science, and studying in different places. Homework problems should be revisited several times over several days, compared to practicing a song until it flows naturally. Looking away from a page and recalling its contents is presented as more effective than highlighting or rereading. Understanding must be combined with practice and repetition in varied circumstances to achieve mastery. The closing remarks emphasize learning how to learn and broadening one's passions.

points.title: 经常自测：打乱闪卡顺序，在不同地点学习
像练歌一样，跨多天反复练习作业题
读后移开视线，主动回忆所学内容
理解结合不同情境下的练习，才能真正掌握
结语：学会学习，拓展自己的兴趣

videos.title: 如何让大脑集中注意力
videos.original_title: How to Get Your Brain to Focus | Chris Bailey | TEDxManchester
videos.creator: Chris Bailey

chapters.title: 从屏幕包围到限制手机：探索注意力变化的起点
chapters.summary: 讲者发现自己从早到晚都被手机、平板、电脑和手表占据注意力，于是进行为期一个月、每天使用手机最多30分钟的实验。约一周后，他感到专注更容易、想法更多，也更常思考未来。这些个人观察促使他查阅研究、拜访专家并继续自我实验，探索科技如何影响注意力。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker introduces his investigation into technology and attention through a personal experiment. After noticing that screens filled his day, from Instagram in bed to an iPad while cooking, computer screens at work, and smartwatch interruptions, he identified his phone as his biggest time sink. He limited all phone use to 30 minutes a day for a month. After roughly a week of adjusting to less stimulation, he reported a longer attention span, more ideas during mind-wandering, and more thoughts and plans about the future. These observations prompted him to read hundreds of research papers, meet focus experts worldwide, and conduct further experiments on himself.

points.title: 日常生活被各种屏幕与通知占据
一个月实验：每天使用手机最多30分钟
适应较低刺激后，专注、想法与未来规划发生变化
从个人观察出发，研究科技如何影响注意力

chapters.title: 注意力为何频繁切换：过度刺激与新奇偏好
chapters.summary: 讲者引用研究称，在电脑前工作、尤其手机在旁时，人们约40秒就会切换注意对象，开着Slack时则降至35秒。他认为分心是大脑过度刺激的表象：大脑渴求零碎信息，并通过“新奇偏好”带来的多巴胺奖励，鼓励人们寻找干扰。他以吃披萨、性爱和查看Facebook的愉悦刺激作类比，解释注意力为何不断跳转。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker discusses attention spans and cites research suggesting that people working at a computer, especially with a phone nearby, switch tasks after about 40 seconds, falling to 35 seconds with Slack open. He argues that distraction is a symptom of overstimulation: the brain craves small pieces of information from social media and email. He describes novelty bias as a dopamine reward mechanism that encourages seeking distraction, comparing the stimulation from checking Facebook with that associated with eating pizza and making love. He concludes that highly stimulated minds keep bouncing between stimulating objects of attention.

points.title: 电脑工作中的注意力切换：40秒与35秒
分心的深层原因：大脑过度刺激并渴求干扰
新奇偏好与多巴胺奖励：披萨、性爱和Facebook的类比
高度刺激状态下，注意力在不同对象间跳转

chapters.title: 每天无聊一小时：降低刺激如何改善专注
chapters.summary: 讲者将从高刺激转入低刺激时的不安称为“无聊”，并介绍连续一个月、每天让自己无聊一小时的实验，包括读条款、等待客服电话、数圆周率中的零和看钟。他发现自己约一周后适应了更低的刺激水平，注意力持续时间也延长了；更容易专注的原因，是大脑不再主动寻找干扰。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker describes boredom as the restlessness felt when moving from high to low stimulation. To explore reducing stimulation further, he spent an hour a day on boring activities for a month, using suggestions from his website readers. Examples included reading iTunes terms and conditions, waiting on hold with Air Canada's baggage claims department, counting zeroes in the first 10,000 digits of pi, and watching a clock. He reports that his mind took about a week to adjust to lower stimulation, relating this to research he cites about needing roughly eight days to fully settle and rest. He also noticed a longer attention span and more effortless focus, which he attributes to his less-stimulated mind no longer seeking distraction.

points.title: 从高刺激转向低刺激时的无聊与不安
实验设计：连续一个月，每天无聊一小时
实验活动：读条款、等客服电话、数零和看钟
约一周适应低刺激，并联系休假研究
专注改善：大脑不再主动寻找干扰

chapters.title: 让思绪漫游：激发创意与规划未来
chapters.summary: 有意让思绪漫游的“分散式专注”，能帮助连接想法、寻找解决办法并规划未来。演讲者引用研究称，漫游时约12%的时间想到过去、28%想到当下、48%想到未来，其余时间思绪空白或不涉及时间。通过洗澡、编织、走路时不看手机等简单活动，为思考留出空间，并及时记录灵感以便日后行动。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker explains how deliberately letting the mind wander, a mode he calls “scatter focus,” can connect ideas, support problem solving, and enable planning. He uses shower inspiration and finding wording for a delicate email after walking to another room as examples. He reports that wandering thoughts concern the past 12% of the time, the present 28%, and the future 48%, calling the tendency toward the future the mind’s prospective bias. The remaining time involves blank thoughts or thoughts not rooted in time. He recommends simple activities that leave attention available, including knitting, bathing, walking without using a phone, waiting in line, and getting a massage, and suggests recording ideas for later action.

points.title: 思绪漫游如何连接想法、产生灵感
有意让思绪漫游：“分散式专注”
漫游的去向：过去、当下与未来偏向
用编织、洗澡和不看手机的步行留出思考空间
及时记录灵感，留待日后行动

chapters.title: 为注意力留白：转变观念与两周减少刺激挑战
chapters.summary: 提出两项注意力观念转变：不再往生活里塞入更多任务，而要像车流需要车距一样，为思绪游走留出空间；分心是大脑刺激过多的症状。建议开展两周减少刺激挑战，观察注意力、想法和计划的变化，并通过设备使用管理、定时断网和短暂体验无聊来实践。最后强调，平静的注意力有助于专注、创造力和生活质量。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker proposes two shifts in thinking about attention: leave more space for mind-wandering instead of fitting in more activity, illustrated by the space between cars on a highway; and view distraction as a symptom of an overstimulated mind. A two-week challenge invites listeners to reduce stimulation and observe changes in attention, ideas, focus, and planning. Suggestions include using device features to reduce screen time, disconnecting from the Internet from 8 p.m. to 8 a.m., taking a weekly technology Sabbath, and spending a few minutes experiencing boredom and letting attention wander. The closing message connects calmer attention with productivity, creativity, and a better life.

points.title: 为生活留出空间：用车距比喻思绪游走所需的余地
分心是大脑受到过多刺激的症状
两周减少刺激挑战：观察专注、想法和计划的变化
实践方法：管理设备使用、定时断网与短暂体验无聊
结语：注意力的状态影响生活的状态

videos.title: 为什么在办公室反而做不成工作
videos.original_title: Why work doesn't happen at work | Jason Fried
videos.creator: Jason Fried

chapters.title: 为什么想把工作做好时，人们很少选择办公室？
chapters.summary: 演讲以“上班时为何难以完成工作”开场：组织投入办公场所和设备，要求员工集中工作，但人们真正想把事情做好时，往往选择其他地点、旅途或清晨、午夜、周末。本段通过这些回答提出办公室投入与实际工作偏好之间的矛盾，尚未解释原因。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker introduces the question of why people struggle to get work done at work. Organizations provide offices, equipment, and shared facilities and require employees or volunteers to work there. Yet, when asked where they go to accomplish something, people tend to name a place or room, a moving vehicle, or a time of day. Examples include porches, kitchens, spare rooms, cafés, libraries, trains, planes, cars, early mornings, late nights, and weekends. The segment highlights how rarely people name the office despite organizations' investment in it, ending by asking why this discrepancy exists without yet explaining its causes.

points.title: 开场问题：为何上班时反而难以完成工作
组织配备办公室，要求员工集中工作
真正想做好工作时，人们会选择哪里？
三类回答及实例：地点、交通工具与工作时段
办公室很少被提及：投入与工作偏好的矛盾

chapters.title: 频繁打断如何让工作日碎片化
chapters.summary: 办公室里的突发事务、提问和会议把工作日切成零碎片段，使人忙了一天却难以完成有意义的工作。设计师、工程师、作家等需要较长且不受干扰的时间深入思考，因此常选择在家、清早、晚间或旅途中工作。讲者用睡眠分阶段、被打断后需要重新开始的类比，说明持续干扰为何妨碍有效工作。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker explains how office interruptions fragment a workday into short stretches, leaving people busy with meetings and miscellaneous tasks but little meaningful work completed. Designers, engineers, writers, programmers, and other creative workers need extended uninterrupted time for careful thought. This helps explain why people work at home, arrive early, stay late, work weekends, or work while traveling. The speaker compares work to sleep: both progress through stages, and interruptions force a restart, making sustained disruption incompatible with good work.

points.title: 突发事务与提问把工作日切成零碎片段
创造性工作需要长时间不受干扰的深入思考
在家、错峰或旅途中工作是为了减少干扰
用睡眠阶段类比工作：被打断后需要重新开始
持续打扰与要求高效工作相互矛盾

chapters.title: 主动分心与被动打断：为何上网不是工作受阻的关键
chapters.summary: 讲者反驳经理因看电视、散步等干扰或无法监督而反对居家工作的理由，强调这些活动由个人决定，办公室的打断则多为被动发生。他质疑封禁社交和视频网站的做法，将偶尔上网比作过去的抽烟休息，认为这不是工作无法完成的关键。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker challenges managers’ objections to working from home, including distractions such as television, walks, and trips to the refrigerator, as well as concerns about not seeing employees work. He distinguishes these voluntary distractions, whose timing people control, from the largely involuntary interruptions in offices. He then criticizes workplace bans on Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube, comparing occasional use to cigarette breaks in the past and arguing that these sites are not the central reason work goes unfinished.

points.title: 经理反对居家工作的理由：生活干扰与无法监督
居家活动可以自主安排，办公室打断多为被动发生
质疑将社交和视频网站视为分心主因并封禁
将偶尔上网比作抽烟休息，指出它并非问题关键

chapters.title: 经理与会议如何打断工作、消耗团队时间
chapters.summary: 讲者将办公室工作的主要干扰归为经理与会议：经理追问进度会打断专注，会议则迫使多人同时停下工作。以10人参加1小时会议为例，说明实际消耗的是10小时的工作时间，并批评原本可由少数人简短沟通的事项被扩展成议程繁多、时长受软件安排影响的会议。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker identifies managers and meetings, called “M&M’s,” as major sources of interruption in offices. Managers disrupt focused work by checking progress at inconvenient moments, while meetings require multiple employees to stop their tasks at once. A meeting attended by ten people for one hour consumes ten hours of collective work time. The speaker argues that matters suitable for a brief discussion among two or three people often become lengthy meetings with crowded agendas and durations shaped by scheduling software.

points.title: 办公室的两大干扰：经理与会议
经理追问进度会打断专注工作
会议迫使多人同时停下手头工作
10人开会1小时，合计消耗10小时
简短沟通被扩展为议程繁多的会议

chapters.title: 设立无交谈时段，让办公室更适合专注工作
chapters.summary: 建议经理通过减少干扰，让办公室成为员工愿意工作的地方。本段具体提出试行“星期四无交谈下午”：先每月安排半天，提供连续4小时的安静工作时间，再考虑增加到隔周或每周一次。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker urges managers to make the office a preferred place for getting work done by reducing interruptions. This segment develops the first proposed change: a no-talking Thursday afternoon, initially on the first Thursday of a month. The speaker argues that four uninterrupted hours are especially valuable for completing work and suggests repeating the quiet afternoon every other week or weekly if the trial proves useful.

points.title: 改善办公环境，让员工愿意来办公室工作
试行星期四无交谈下午，从每月半天开始
连续4小时不受干扰的工作时间有何价值
尝试将安静下午增加到隔周或每周一次

chapters.title: 用可自主安排的沟通方式减少工作打断
chapters.summary: 建议将面对面交谈、会议等主动交流转为电子邮件、即时通讯或协作工具，让自己选择查看信息的时机。工作像睡眠一样需要分阶段铺垫，而真正需要立即处理的急事很少，因此可鼓励经理采用这些工具来协调工作节奏。
chapters.english_summary: This unit recommends shifting from face-to-face conversations and meetings to more passive communication through email, instant messaging, and collaboration tools. It discusses how these tools can also be distracting, while emphasizing personal choice over when to engage with them and the continuing need to respond to managers. It compares work to sleep as a process that proceeds in stages, suggests checking messages at suitable times, and notes that few issues require immediate action. It closes by discussing managers encouraging these tools and aligning work rhythms.

points.title: 从面对面交流转向邮件、即时通讯与协作工具
沟通工具是否造成干扰与个人选择有关
工作需要分阶段推进，可适时查看消息
真正需要立即处理的急事很少
经理鼓励使用沟通工具并协调工作步调

chapters.title: 取消一次会议，把时间还给实质工作
chapters.summary: 最后一条建议是：有权决定时，直接取消下一场会议，而非改期。以周一会议为例，讲者认为取消后事情仍可能顺利进行，大家也能拥有更自由的早晨，并发现一些原以为必须处理的事项并非必要。结尾呼吁管理者思考这些建议，与其裁员，不如给员工更多时间做实质工作。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker's final recommendation is to cancel the next meeting outright, if one has the authority, rather than reschedule it. Using a Monday morning meeting as an example, the speaker argues that things may still run smoothly without the planned discussions and decisions, giving people a freer morning and revealing that some supposedly essential tasks may be unnecessary. The talk closes by asking managers, businesspeople, and organizers to consider the three recommendations and give people more time for substantive work rather than cut staff, followed by thanks and applause.

points.title: 有决定权时，取消下一场会议而非改期
以周一早晨为例：省去讨论与决定，事情仍可能顺利
腾出更自由的早晨，重新判断哪些事必须做
结尾呼吁：与其裁员，不如增加实质工作的时间

videos.title: 如何掌控自己的空闲时间
videos.original_title: How to gain control of your free time | Laura Vanderkam | TED
videos.creator: Laura Vanderkam

chapters.title: 时间管理的关键：先确定重要的事，再安排时间
chapters.summary: 讲者质疑从日常活动中零碎省时的思路，主张先建立想要的生活，再调整时间安排。她通过忙碌女性花七小时处理热水器漏水，以及企业主抽空远足的经历，说明时间安排会随优先事项改变。“没有时间”通常意味着事情不是首要任务；虽然选择可能带来后果，人仍能选择值得投入时间的事。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker challenges the idea that saving small amounts of time from everyday activities is the way to build the life one wants. After discussing shortcuts such as skipping television commercials, she introduces a time-diary project documenting 1,001 days in the lives of busy women. One participant found seven hours to deal with a broken water heater and a flooded basement, illustrating how schedules adjust to priorities. A business owner with twelve employees and six children chose to go hiking on a beautiful morning and described her time as a matter of choice. The speaker reframes 'I don't have time' as 'It's not a priority,' using an example of being offered $100,000 to dust blinds. She acknowledges that choices can have serious consequences while emphasizing the ability to spend time on worthwhile things.

points.title: 零碎省时的局限：跳过电视广告与减少看电视
转换思路：先建立想要的生活，再安排时间
热水器漏水案例：忙碌的一周仍能腾出七小时
企业主远足的选择：时间投入取决于优先事项
百叶窗除尘的例子：重新理解“没有时间”与选择

chapters.title: 找出重要目标，拆解任务并优先排入日程
chapters.summary: 通过预写明年的年度绩效评估和家庭假日信件，分别找出事业与个人生活中最重要的三到五件事，形成六到十个目标。把目标拆成可执行的阶段性任务，如写家族传记或参加五千米比赛，再像处理坏掉的热水器一样优先安排。建议周五下午列出事业、人际关系、个人三类事项，每类两到三件，规划下周的行动。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how to identify priorities and schedule them first. Imagine it is the end of next year and write a performance review naming three to five achievements that made it an outstanding professional year. Do the same for personal life by drafting next year's family holiday letter, identifying three to five meaningful accomplishments. Turn the resulting six to ten goals into actionable steps. Examples include reading family histories and arranging interviews with relatives to write a family biography, or registering for a 5K race, making a training plan, and finding running shoes. Treat priorities like a broken water heater and put them into the calendar first. Friday afternoon is suggested as a low-opportunity-cost time to plan: list two or three priorities in each of three categories—career, relationships, and self—and decide how to schedule them for the following week.

points.title: 预写明年绩效评估，找出三到五项事业目标
预写家庭假日信件，找出个人生活的重要目标
拆解目标：家族传记与五千米比赛的行动步骤
像处理坏掉的热水器一样，把首要事项优先排入日程
周五列出事业、人际关系、个人三类事项，规划下周

chapters.title: 从每周168小时中寻找重要事情的时间
chapters.summary: 讲者先承认照顾孩子等现实负担会使安排时间更困难，再以每周168小时为基础，扣除工作和睡眠时间，说明仍有时间安排其他事情。她引用自报工时与工作日记存在差距的研究，鼓励人们重新审视忙碌程度，为陪伴孩子、备考、锻炼或志愿服务寻找时间。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker acknowledges that complex lives and childcare responsibilities can make scheduling difficult. Using a 168-hour week, she considers time remaining after work and sleep under different working-hour scenarios. She cites a study comparing estimated working hours with work diaries, reporting a 25-hour discrepancy among people claiming to work more than 75 hours. She argues that even people working long hours can find time for priorities such as spending time with children, preparing for exams, exercising, or volunteering.

points.title: 承认照顾孩子等现实负担带来的时间困难
以每周168小时估算工作和睡眠以外的时间
自报工作时间与实际工作日记可能存在差距
为陪伴孩子、备考、锻炼和志愿服务寻找时间

chapters.title: 利用零星时间，把重要的事放进生活
chapters.summary: 零星时间也能带来快乐：通勤时阅读、工作间隙冥想或祷告，无法共进家庭晚餐时尝试家庭早餐。回顾全部时间，寻找做想做之事的机会；即使忙碌，也能关注重要的事，用已有时间创造想要的生活。最后致谢结束演讲。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker closes by explaining that small pockets of time can provide enjoyment and room for meaningful activities. Examples include reading during a commute, finding library books for a journey involving two buses and a subway, meditating or praying during work breaks, and trying a family breakfast when work prevents a family dinner. The conclusion encourages looking across one's available time, finding opportunities for desired activities, and focusing on what matters to create the life one wants. The talk ends with thanks and applause.

points.title: 空闲片刻常被手机、邮件和电视占据
利用通勤时间阅读，收获零星快乐
工作间隙冥想或祷告，家庭早餐替代晚餐
审视全部时间，寻找做想做之事的机会
关注重要的事，用已有时间创造想要的生活

videos.title: 打造第二大脑
videos.original_title: Tiago Forte | Building a Second Brain | Talks at Google
videos.creator: Tiago Forte

chapters.title: “第二大脑”的缘起：失忆经历与外部支持系统
chapters.summary: 主持人介绍《打造第二大脑》作者 Tiago Forte。他回顾大学期间出现的长期喉颈疼痛，以及服药后经历的严重短期记忆丧失，包括忘记曾去过莫斯科。这段经历让他意识到记忆对个人身份的重要性，也促使他依靠外部支持系统，在大脑和身体受限时支撑生活与事业目标。
chapters.english_summary: Charlene Wang introduces Tiago Forte, author of Building a Second Brain. Forte recounts his life as a business student and Apple Store employee in 2007, followed by persistent throat and neck pain that specialists could not explain. He describes taking medication and experiencing severe short-term memory loss, illustrated by forgetting a trip to Moscow while serving in the Peace Corps in eastern Ukraine. He reflects on the choice between pain relief and access to memory, the role of memories in personal identity, and his need to rely on external support systems to pursue his life and career goals when his brain and body could not support sustained effort. The segment introduces the personal origins of his work; it does not yet explain a practical system.

points.title: 开场介绍：Tiago Forte 与《打造第二大脑》
2007 年的生活：商科学业与苹果商店工作
持续喉颈疼痛与多年求医经历
服药后的记忆丧失：忘记莫斯科之旅
从珍视记忆到依靠外部支持系统

chapters.title: 从信息过载到延展认知：用外部工具扩展心智
chapters.summary: 讲者认为，现代信息量已超出大脑的处理能力，并可能共同导致犹豫、分心、焦虑和拖延。他介绍延展认知领域及《延展心智》一书，以猴子用耙子取物后大脑重新映射身体边界的研究，说明外部工具如何融入认知。随后结合丢失手机、断网无法搜索的体验，以及眼镜、鞋和手表的类比，提出人们需要能扩展心智能力的辅助工具。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker argues that modern information overload exceeds the brain's capacity and may underlie indecision, distraction, stress, anxiety, and procrastination. He introduces Extended Cognition and recommends Annie Murphy Paul's The Extended Mind. He describes a study in which monkeys used a rake to retrieve an object, and brain scans indicated that their body maps incorporated the tool. He connects this account to smartphones, the panic of losing a phone, and the disruption of being unable to search Google without internet access. Comparing technology to prosthetic devices, with glasses, shoes, and watches as examples, he argues for a device that extends the mind's capabilities to meet the demands of modern life.

points.title: 信息过载与大脑承受能力的冲突
认识延展认知与《延展心智》
猴子用耙子取物：工具进入身体映射
手机与搜索如何成为认知的一部分
从眼镜、鞋和手表谈心智辅助工具

chapters.title: 什么是第二大脑：面向终身学习的笔记系统
chapters.summary: 第二大脑并非必须依赖未来科技，而是对日常记笔记方式的增强：在大脑之外，用纸张或软件长期保存对自己重要、值得重访和反思的信息，形成学习、发现与研究的个人档案，支持持续学习、创造和成长。
chapters.english_summary: Tiago Forte explains that a second brain does not require futuristic technology: it builds on the familiar practice of taking notes using paper or existing software. He frames it as reinventing notetaking for the modern connected age, turning occasional scribbles into a lifelong practice of learning, creating, and producing. In response to Charlene Wang's question, he defines a second brain as a trusted place outside the brain for long-term storage of personally meaningful information to revisit and reflect on. It is an archive of learning, discoveries, and research that extends beyond a single test, paper, or project. He personally prefers using software.

points.title: 从未来科技的想象回到日常记笔记
为互联时代重塑笔记，让它支持终身学习与创造
第二大脑的定义：在大脑之外长期保存重要信息
建立跨越单次任务的终身学习档案
讲者个人偏好用软件建立第二大脑

chapters.title: 用第二大脑保存与复用思考成果，提升工作效率
chapters.summary: 第二大脑在职业与业务中尤其有价值：把研究、头脑风暴、决策和方案评估中形成的笔记、要点与行动步骤保存下来，遇到类似会议或问题时即可复用。长期积累知识会产生复利，减少重复思考，为解决更复杂、更有趣的问题腾出时间和精力。
chapters.english_summary: Tiago Forte explains how a second brain can make professionals more effective at work. Knowledge workers invest scarce attention in brainstorming, research, decisions, and evaluating options. Saving the resulting notes, bullet points, and action steps allows them to revisit their best thinking in similar meetings or situations instead of repeating the work. Over time, this accumulation of knowledge compounds like an investment, freeing time and mental capacity for more interesting, unusual, and complex problems.

points.title: 第二大脑在职业与业务中的应用价值
知识工作需要投入宝贵的注意力
保存思考形成的笔记、要点与行动步骤
遇到类似情境时复用已有思考
通过知识复利，为复杂问题腾出精力

chapters.title: 第二大脑实演：用笔记组织项目、保存资料与记住细节
chapters.summary: Tiago 展示自己使用十年的 Evernote：按当前项目、责任领域和兴趣主题组织笔记，保存文字、图片、链接与附件。约七千条笔记平均每天只需积累两条，多数仅三五十词。他以 Readwise 自动导入的阅读划线、历史书单、视频大纲及团队招聘讨论记录为例，说明如何借助软件保存未来可能用到的信息，减轻记忆细节的负担。
chapters.english_summary: Tiago Forte demonstrates his second brain in Evernote, while noting that other note-taking apps can also be used. He organizes notebooks around active projects, areas of responsibility, and interests, with notes containing text, images, links, and attachments. His roughly 7,000 notes accumulated over ten years amount to about two per day, and most are only 30–50 words. Examples include highlights from The Whole-Brain Child automatically imported through Readwise, a spreadsheet of historically important books saved for possible future use, a YouTube video outline, and brief notes from team calls about hiring. He explains how software preserves details he would otherwise forget.

points.title: 工具选择：用 Evernote 或其他笔记软件搭建第二大脑
组织方式：按项目、责任领域与兴趣主题分类
笔记形式与积累：短小记录，平均每天两条
资料保存实例：自动导入阅读划线，收藏未来可能有用的书单
工作记录实例：用视频大纲与招聘讨论笔记留住细节

chapters.title: 第二大脑如何避免信息囤积：从轻松收集到主动筛选
chapters.summary: 回应记录过多是否影响查找的问题，Tiago指出，数字工具已让收集变得容易，笔记的瓶颈转向整理、提炼与表达。他介绍CODE四步骤，用免费购物导致家中堆满物品的比喻说明数字囤积，并以自己每天仅记录两件事为例，强调逐步提高筛选标准，减少收集，反思“信息越多越好”的惯性。
chapters.english_summary: Responding to an audience question about whether recording every brainstorming session makes a second brain difficult to search, Tiago Forte explains that digital tools have shifted the bottleneck from capturing notes to processing them. Bookmarks and integrations such as Readwise make capture easy. He introduces CODE: Capture, Organize, Distill, and Express, emphasizing the need to filter large collections into a manageable amount for review and use. He compares digital hoarding to taking everything from a free store until the house is full, and describes becoming more selective over time, personally recording about two things a day in a few bullet points. He challenges assumptions inherited from information scarcity, including that more information is always better and that valuable information must be elsewhere, and emphasizes limiting accumulation and capturing less.

points.title: 观众提问：记录太多会不会让信息难以查找？
数字工具让收集更容易，笔记瓶颈转向后续处理
CODE四步骤：收集、整理、提炼与表达
从免费购物的比喻理解数字囤积，逐步减少记录
反思“信息越多越好”，主动限制积累

chapters.title: 随时捕捉想法：笔记工具的移动端为何重要
chapters.summary: 针对社交或其他活动中是否会用手机记笔记的问题，Tiago 强调移动端至关重要。洗澡后想到点子、开车抵达目的地或开会时，都可能需要即时记录。因此，第二大脑应用应具备流畅、快捷、使用阻力小的移动端。
chapters.english_summary: Asked whether he uses his phone to capture notes while socializing or engaged in other activities, Tiago Forte strongly affirms the importance of mobile functionality. He expects more notes to be captured on the go and in the moment, such as after a shower, upon arriving somewhere after driving, or during a meeting. With mobile devices taking a growing share of device usage, he identifies a seamless, quick, frictionless mobile app as a key criterion for a second brain tool.

points.title: 提问：社交或活动中是否用手机记录笔记
移动端至关重要，更多笔记会在当下随手记录
记录场景：洗澡后、开车抵达后及会议中
选用第二大脑工具，应看重移动端的流畅与快捷

chapters.title: CODE 工作流：把信息转化为解决问题的成果
chapters.summary: 第二大脑的核心是使用信息的习惯。CODE 通过捕捉、组织、提炼和表达，把日常信息转化为实际成果。Tiago 以婴儿睡眠问题为例，展示如何保存书中划线、归入项目、筛选适龄建议，最终制作一页纸睡眠计划；表达不必公开发布，也可以是解决个人问题的具体产物。
chapters.english_summary: Tiago Forte explains CODE as a workflow of Capture, Organize, Distill, and Express, emphasizing that a second brain depends on habits for using information. He demonstrates the workflow through his infant son's sleep problem: saving highlights from The Happy Sleeper into a note, moving it into a sleep-training project folder, bolding advice relevant to his son's current age and needs, and turning those points into a one-page paper sleep plan posted outside the bedroom. Expression means creating a concrete artifact that helps solve a problem and does not require public publication.

points.title: CODE 的核心：用习惯推动信息走向成果
捕捉：为解决孩子睡眠问题保存阅读划线
组织：把笔记移入睡眠训练项目
提炼：标出适合当前年龄与问题的建议
表达：制作可在夜间查看的一页纸睡眠计划

chapters.title: 笔记如何保留语境，并通过跨领域重组产生创意
chapters.summary: 回答记录信息时如何保留语境：按需摘取内容并保存来源，方便日后回查细节与例外。同时，原始语境不必限制想法的应用，例如将有机种植的思路迁移到粉丝增长。把不同领域的材料集中存放，有助于重组与表达；借鉴时应认真引用来源，可用文献管理工具追踪资料。
chapters.english_summary: In response to a question about preserving context when recording information, Tiago Forte recommends saving the context needed along with a source link or citation, then returning to the source for details, nuances, and exceptions. He also questions whether the original context must determine an idea's use, illustrating cross-pollination with an idea from organic gardening applied to growing an online following. Keeping diverse material together in a second brain can encourage unexpected combinations and creative expression. He describes creativity as recombination and emphasizes citing sources, mentioning Mendeley and Zotero as tools for tracking research.

points.title: 按需保留语境与来源，方便回查细节
松动原始语境：将有机种植思路用于粉丝增长
集中存放不同领域的想法，促进组合与突破
通过重组已有材料形成创意表达
认真引用来源，并用文献管理工具追踪资料

chapters.title: 记录私人想法的焦虑：第二大脑也是个人成长
chapters.summary: 回应写下私人想法时担心被他人看到和评价的焦虑，Tiago指出，建立第二大脑遇到的障碍往往来自情绪，包括隐私与安全担忧、害怕批评、怀疑自身想法的价值，以及认为知识管理只适合某些职业。他强调每个人的故事和想法都有价值，需要为自己争取空间、面对成长挑战；生产力实践与个人成长密不可分。
chapters.english_summary: Responding to a question about anxiety over externalizing private thoughts and being judged if others read them, Tiago Forte explains that building a second brain quickly becomes a personal growth experience. Obstacles include fears about privacy, security, sharing ideas, and criticism, as well as limiting beliefs about whether one's ideas matter. He gives the example of a product manager believing knowledge management is only for scientists and researchers. He affirms the value of everyone's stories and ideas and encourages people to stand up for themselves and work through these challenges. Charlene Wang adds that productivity and personal growth cannot be separated.

points.title: 提问：担心私人想法被看到和负面评价
建立第二大脑的障碍往往来自情绪
隐私、安全与表达想法时的恐惧
限制性信念：自己的想法有价值吗，职业适合知识管理吗
肯定自身价值，面对与生产力实践相伴的成长挑战

chapters.title: 用第二大脑学习技术技能：复用资料与外化知识
chapters.summary: 回应如何用第二大脑学习技术技能，Tiago以软件工程师的实践为例，说明代码片段、Stack Overflow、维基、知识库和文档如何支持学习与解决问题。将信息移到大脑之外并加以整理，有助于客观审视、持续改进，以及利用他人的想法和贡献。
chapters.english_summary: In response to a question about applying Building a Second Brain to learning technical skills, Tiago describes how software engineers influenced his approach. He highlights reusing code snippets, finding solutions on Stack Overflow, and relying on wikis, knowledge bases, and documentation. He explains that any skill involving absorbing, interpreting, and structuring information benefits from an external place to work with it, enabling clearer examination, iteration, innovation, and the use of others' ideas and contributions.

points.title: 提问：如何用第二大脑学习以参考资料为主的技术技能
软件工程师的启发：复用代码片段、知识库与文档
文档和参考资料是学习技术技能的核心支撑
将信息外化，便于审视、迭代并吸收他人贡献

chapters.title: 用30天笔记实验开始建立第二大脑
chapters.summary: 先用手机自带的笔记应用，每天保存一条具有长期价值的想法，不必纠结工具选择。30天后回顾积累的知识素材，尝试组合、复用它们来解决问题，减少重复思考。如果觉得有用，就继续积累，也可增加到每天两条。
chapters.english_summary: Tiago Forte suggests a 30-day experiment as an easy first step toward building a second brain, while noting that the approach is not a universal solution and may suit people who handle large amounts of information or work extensively on computers. Use a phone's built-in notes app, such as Apple Notes or Google Keep, and save one evergreen idea each day, including a theory, framework, quote, or approach. After 30 days, review the accumulated knowledge assets and consider how to reuse and combine them like LEGO blocks to solve problems, answer questions, and reduce repeated thinking. Continue if the experiment proves valuable, optionally increasing to two notes a day and accumulating over 700 notes in a year.

points.title: 先试30天，判断第二大脑是否适合自己
使用手机自带笔记应用，避免陷入选工具的纠结
每天记录一条有长期价值的想法
30天后回顾并组合知识素材，解决实际问题
有收获就继续积累，可增加到每天两条

chapters.title: 如何检索第二大脑：在项目启动时调用已有笔记
chapters.summary: Tiago 回答何时回看第二大脑：主要依靠关键词和模糊搜索找回笔记，文件夹作为补充；他本人没有固定复习习惯，而是在项目启动时，结合目标、时间和预算检索已有思考。以企业网站改版获批为例，他说明如何借助旧笔记避免从零开始，并强调从“以备万一”转向机会出现时灵活调用知识。
chapters.english_summary: Tiago Forte answers a question about how often he revisits his second brain. He emphasizes keyword search, describes finding Evernote notes from one or two remembered words, and explains how fuzzy search can handle approximate terms and typos. He sees folders as a supplement to search. He has no regular note-review routine and instead retrieves material when a project begins. Using an approved business website redesign as an example, he explains how searching existing notes with the project's timeline, budget, and success criteria in mind lets past thinking inform the work. The discussion then contrasts just-in-case preparation with just-in-time responses to emerging opportunities, supported by a prepared second brain.

points.title: 用关键词和模糊搜索找回笔记，文件夹辅助检索
不必为记忆而固定复习：讲者没有例行回顾习惯
项目启动是检索时机：以网站改版获批为例
结合项目条件查找已有笔记，复用过去的思考
从“以备万一”转向机会出现时及时调用知识

chapters.title: PARA 信息整理法：按行动性分类，把注意力留给当前项目
chapters.summary: Tiago 介绍 PARA 的四类信息：有短期目标的项目、持续承担的责任领域、可能有用的资源，以及不再需要行动的归档。它按行动性而非学科分类，并可在不同软件中保持一致结构。他用百条笔记的注意力分配和炉上煮面的比喻，说明应优先关注当前项目；已完成的项目或不再关注的领域则移入归档，保留资料而不干扰当前工作。
chapters.english_summary: Tiago Forte explains PARA as a framework for organizing notes and files into Projects with short-term outcomes, Areas of ongoing responsibility, Resources containing potentially useful reference material, and Archives for items from the other categories that are no longer actionable. He contrasts organizing by actionability with organizing by broad subjects and describes maintaining the same structure across Evernote, Google Drive, ClickUp, and calendars. Using 100 notes and an 80/20-style allocation of attention, followed by a boiling-pasta analogy, he argues that active projects and deadlines deserve most attention. Finished projects and areas no longer pursued are archived. He compares archives to cold storage: material remains available for future use without cluttering the workspace or distracting from current priorities.

points.title: PARA 四类：项目、责任领域、资源与归档
按行动性排序，而非按学科分类
在不同软件中保持相同的组织结构
用笔记分配与煮面比喻说明为何优先关注项目
归档已结束或不再关注的事项，避免干扰当前工作

chapters.title: 结语：主动整理已有信息，把答案付诸行动
chapters.summary: Tiago以自身健康经历作结：他索取并数字化病历，整理、批注和对比不同医生的建议，认识到自己需要改善日常照护，并与医生合作制定健康习惯，最终改善症状。他鼓励观众主动利用身边已有的信息，通过捕捉、组织、提炼和表达将其转化为行动。主持人最后推荐《Building a Second Brain》并致谢。
chapters.english_summary: In his closing remarks, Tiago Forte completes his personal health story. After consulting numerous doctors, he obtained his full medical records, digitized them, and annotated, organized, linked, and compared their advice. He concluded that his condition required changes in nutrition, sleep, self-care, and mental health, and developed simple health habits with his doctor's input that ultimately helped resolve his symptoms. He encourages viewers to consider whether answers to their own problems already exist in their records, journals, relationships, workplace resources, or online, and to take ownership by capturing, organizing, distilling, and expressing that information through action. Charlene closes by recommending Building a Second Brain and thanking Tiago.

points.title: 从等待治愈到主动承担健康管理责任
数字化病历，整理并比较医生的建议
结合整体信息，与医生合作改善日常健康习惯
寻找身边已有的答案，将信息整理并付诸行动
推荐《Building a Second Brain》与结束致谢

videos.title: 拖延者的大脑在想什么
videos.original_title: Inside the Mind of a Master Procrastinator | Tim Urban | TED
videos.creator: Tim Urban

chapters.title: 拖延症开场：三天赶完90页毕业论文
chapters.summary: 讲者以大学写论文的经历开场，对比分摊任务的理想计划与一拖再拖的实际表现。他原本打算用一年逐步完成90页毕业论文，却拖到截止前三天才动笔，最终连续熬夜赶交，论文质量很差。结尾所谓学校来电称赞的情节只是笑话。
chapters.english_summary: In this opening anecdote, the speaker contrasts a student's steady writing schedule with his own repeated procrastination. He planned to complete a 90-page thesis gradually over a year but kept postponing the work until only three days remained. He then wrote all 90 pages in 72 hours, stayed up for two consecutive nights, and submitted just before the deadline. He jokes that the university called to praise the thesis, then explicitly reveals that the call never happened and that the thesis was very poor.

points.title: 写论文的理想进度与实际拖延
90页毕业论文的一年分阶段计划
计划不断修改，仍迟迟没有动笔
截止前三天赶写90页并交稿
学校称赞只是笑话，论文实际很差

chapters.title: 拖延的内心冲突：即时满足猴子与理性决策者
chapters.summary: 讲者用“即时满足猴子”和“理性决策制定者”比喻拖延者的内心冲突：前者追求眼前的简单快乐，让人读闲闻、翻冰箱、不断刷视频；后者考虑未来与长期价值。两者在合理休息时可以一致，但面对困难却值得做的事时会冲突，使拖延者进入“黑暗的操场”：在不该休闲时娱乐，并伴随内疚、恐惧、焦虑和自我憎恨。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker introduces his attempt to explain procrastination and uses a humorous comparison of brains to present the Rational Decision-Maker and the Instant Gratification Monkey. The monkey takes control when productive work should begin, diverting attention to a Wikipedia scandal article, repeated refrigerator checks, and a chain of videos from Richard Feynman discussing magnetism to an interview with Justin Bieber's mother. It cares only about what is easy and fun in the present, while the rational decision-maker considers the future, the bigger picture, and long-term plans. They can agree on eating, sleeping, and deserved leisure, but conflict when worthwhile tasks are difficult or unpleasant. The speaker calls leisure at inappropriate times the Dark Playground, where enjoyment is accompanied by guilt, fear, anxiety, and self-hatred.

points.title: 用两种大脑的幽默对比引出“即时满足猴子”
猴子接管方向盘：读闲闻、翻冰箱与不断刷视频
即时满足猴子只关心当下的简单与快乐
理性决策者考虑未来，两者在休息与困难任务上的异同
“黑暗的操场”：不合时宜的娱乐与负面感受

chapters.title: 恐慌怪兽如何让拖延者开始行动
chapters.summary: 用“恐慌怪兽”解释拖延者为何会在截止期或严重后果逼近时开始行动：恐慌吓退猴子，让理性的决策制定者重新掌控。讲者以准备TED演讲时沉迷谷歌地球、直到演讲者名单公布才动手，以及论文拖延后通宵写作的例子，说明三种角色构成的拖延系统。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the Panic Monster's role in procrastination. Usually dormant, it wakes when a deadline approaches or public embarrassment, career disaster, or other frightening consequences loom. It is the only thing the monkey fears, allowing the rational decision-maker to regain control. The speaker describes accepting a TED invitation six months ahead, spending two and a half hours exploring India in Google Earth instead of preparing, and finally starting after seeing his face on the published speaker list a month before the event. He also describes struggling for two weeks to start a paper, then writing eight pages overnight. The three characters form a flawed but functional procrastination system.

points.title: 恐慌怪兽：截止期或可怕后果逼近时醒来
TED备稿拖延：用谷歌地球探索印度
演讲者名单公布，恐慌促使准备启动
论文拖延两周后，通宵写出八页
三种角色构成拖延者的系统

chapters.title: 没有截止期的拖延：为何让人迟迟无法追逐梦想
chapters.summary: 讲者从读者来信中的挫败感出发，区分有截止期与无截止期的拖延：前者会被“恐慌怪兽”推动，后者却可能无限延续，影响创业、健康、家庭与亲密关系，让人连追逐梦想都无法开始。最后用每格代表一周的90岁生命日历，提醒大家审视正在拖延的重要事情，意识到即时满足的诱惑并尽早行动。
chapters.english_summary: Drawing on thousands of reader emails, the speaker distinguishes procrastination with deadlines from procrastination without them. Deadlines activate the metaphorical Panic Monster and limit delays, while goals without deadlines—such as starting a business, pursuing art, visiting family, maintaining health, or improving or leaving a relationship—can be postponed indefinitely. This quieter, long-term procrastination can cause unhappiness, guilt, and the feeling of being a spectator in one's own life, unable even to begin pursuing dreams. The speaker argues that everyone procrastinates and closes with a life calendar representing 90 years in weekly boxes, encouraging reflection on what we are postponing, awareness of the Instant Gratification Monkey, and action soon.

points.title: 读者来信：拖延带来的沉重挫败感
两种拖延：截止期能否唤醒“恐慌怪兽”
长期拖延的代价：成为生活的旁观者
人人都会拖延，尤其是没有截止期的事
生命日历：审视拖延的重要事情并尽早行动

videos.title: 微积分的本质：从圆的面积出发
videos.original_title: The essence of calculus
videos.creator: 3Blue1Brown

chapters.title: 从圆的面积理解积分：薄圆环求和如何变成图像下面积
chapters.summary: 先介绍以直观方式理解微积分的系列目标，再以半径为3的圆为例，将圆拆成同心薄圆环，用2πr·dr近似各环面积。把这些面积对应为直线下的窄矩形，随着dr减小，矩形总面积趋近三角形面积，得到圆面积πR²。最后归纳从小量求和到图像下面积的思路，并以速度乘微小时间求路程说明其应用。
chapters.english_summary: The unit opens with the series goal of developing visual understanding of calculus rather than memorizing rules. It then derives the area of a circle, initially of radius 3, by slicing it into concentric rings. Each ring is approximated by a rectangle of area 2πr·dr, with the approximation improving as dr decreases. Arranging these rectangles beneath the line y = 2πr turns their sum into an approximation of a triangular area, yielding πR² for a circle of radius R. The explanation emphasizes that dr determines both rectangle width and the spacing of radius values, and that finer sums approach the exact area under the graph. It briefly extends this reasoning to estimating distance traveled by summing velocity times small time intervals.

points.title: 系列目标：用直观思考理解微积分核心思想的来源
拆分同心圆环，用2πr·dr近似每个薄环的面积
将薄环对应为直线下的矩形，得到圆面积πR²
从近似到精确：dr同时决定小量大小与取值间隔
推广小量求和思路：由速度和微小时间估算路程

chapters.title: 从曲线下面积到导数：理解微积分基本定理
chapters.summary: 以抛物线 x² 下从 0 到可变端点 x 的面积函数为例，引出积分。通过把新增的窄条面积近似为矩形，说明面积变化量与输入变化量之比趋近于曲线高度，并由此介绍导数及其反求积分的作用，揭示微积分基本定理所连接的积分与导数关系。
chapters.english_summary: Introduces an integral as the function giving the area under x² from 0 to a variable endpoint x, motivated by the area from 0 to 3 and practical problems involving sums of many small quantities. A small increase dx adds a thin strip approximated by a rectangle of height x² and width dx, so dA/dx approaches x² as dx shrinks. Nearby inputs 3 and 3.001 illustrate the change ratio. The discussion generalizes this relationship to area functions, defines the derivative as the limiting ratio of output change to input change, and describes it as sensitivity to small input changes. It explains how knowing a derivative can help recover an unknown area function and names the connection between integration and differentiation the fundamental theorem of calculus. The unit closes with a preview of further exploration in the series.

points.title: 用可变端点定义 x² 的面积函数与积分
用窄矩形近似新增面积，得到变化量之比
用 3 与 3.001 的邻近输入理解面积变化
推广面积变化关系，并引出导数的极限含义
由导数反求积分与微积分基本定理

chapters.title: 片尾致谢：支持者的贡献与社区回馈
chapters.summary: 感谢 Patreon 支持者提供资金和制作建议，说明支持者可提前观看本系列及未来同类系列，并以新视频首月不投放广告回馈社区。最后感谢观众让创作得以持续。
chapters.english_summary: The closing remarks thank Patreon supporters for financial backing and suggestions during the series' development. Supporters received early access and will continue to receive it for future essence-of series. New videos remain ad-free for their first month as a thank-you to the community, and the creator thanks viewers for making this work possible.

points.title: 感谢支持者的资金支持与制作建议
支持者可提前观看本系列及未来同类系列
新视频首月不投放广告，回馈社区
感谢观众让视频创作得以持续

videos.title: 好设计如何让人愉悦
videos.original_title: The three ways that good design makes you happy | Don Norman
videos.creator: TED

chapters.title: 情感化设计：美感、实用与乐趣如何打动人
chapters.summary: 讲者通过史达克果汁机、日本小刀、互动乒乓球桌、Google分页和Mini Cooper，探讨产品外观、使用感受与趣味带来的情感吸引力。美可以激发拥有欲，也能与实用兼容；细腻的设计可能带来潜意识的愉悦，令人喜爱的体验也可能让人接受产品的缺陷。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker explores beauty, usability, fun, and emotional appeal through several design examples: a gold-plated Philippe Starck juicer displayed rather than used for juice; a Japanese knife admired for its shape, balance, sharpness, and comfortable use; an MIT Media Lab ping-pong table with projected fish and ripples responding to ball impacts; Google's repeated-O pagination as a subtle source of subconscious pleasure, followed by an anecdote about search rankings changing when a conjunction is omitted; and a Mini Cooper whose playful interior and enjoyable driving experience appeal despite its flaws. He mentions a three-part theory of emotion but does not explain its components in this unit.

points.title: 史达克果汁机：美感与趣味激发拥有欲
日本小刀：外形、握感与实用兼具
互动乒乓球桌：击球触发水波与游鱼反应
Google分页：细腻设计带来的潜意识愉悦
Mini Cooper：令人愉悦的体验让缺陷变得可接受

chapters.title: 情绪如何影响思考：焦虑促进专注，快乐激发创意
chapters.summary: 通过地面与高空木板的设想，说明恐惧和焦虑会改变思考方式，并以演讲前的紧张说明焦虑有助于集中注意力。随后介绍两根绳子的实验：第一组学生未能完成任务，另一组吃糖、心情改善后解决了问题。讲者据此对比焦虑时的深度优先思考与快乐时的广度优先思考，说明头脑风暴有利于产生创意，而落实工作也需要时间安排和一定的焦虑感。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker uses an imagined plank on the floor versus 300 feet above the ground to explain how fear and anxiety change thinking, and cites pre-talk nervousness as a way anxiety can support concentration. An experiment attributed to psychologist Alice Isen asks students to tie together two ropes they cannot reach simultaneously. The first group fails, while another group solves the task after receiving candy and feeling somewhat happier; the solution itself is not described. The speaker contrasts focused, depth-first thinking under anxiety with broader, breadth-first thinking when happy, connects a playful and noncritical brainstorming atmosphere to unusual ideas, and argues that completing work also requires a schedule and some anxiety.

points.title: 木板与演讲紧张的例子：恐惧和焦虑改变注意力
两根绳子的实验：第一组学生未能完成任务
吃糖改善心情后，另一组学生解决了问题
焦虑与快乐对应不同的思考方式
头脑风暴激发创意，完成工作还需时间安排

chapters.title: 本能层面的情感与设计吸引力
chapters.summary: 解释演化如何塑造人对颜色、味道、声音、温度及面孔的本能好恶，以及设计如何通过字体、颜色和外观表达情感。以经常出故障却仍受喜爱的1963年猎豹汽车，以及喝完水后被保留作装饰或再次使用的别致水罐，说明外观带来的本能吸引力。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains perceptual processing and instinctive emotional preferences shaped by evolution, including attraction to vivid colors and symmetrical faces, and aversion to bitterness, noise, extreme temperatures, scolding voices, and frowning faces. It connects these preferences to design choices such as typography and color. Examples include a beautiful 1963 car that owners love despite frequent breakdowns, and a distinctive water container kept for decoration or refilled after its original contents are consumed, illustrating the instinctive appeal of appearance.

points.title: 演化塑造对鲜艳颜色的偏好：吃水果与传播种子
感官与面孔的本能好恶
通过字体和颜色表达情感
汽车案例：经常出故障仍因美感受喜爱
水罐案例：别致外观让人保留并再次使用

chapters.title: 行为层设计：掌控感、感官体验与产品的情感交流
chapters.summary: 介绍熟练行为的潜意识特征，指出行为设计应让使用者感到一切尽在掌控。通过小刀、汽车和淋浴头说明掌控感与感官体验，再以可改变摆放姿态的茶壶解释泡茶控制及状态传达，并讨论情感判断如何关联安全感、行动和交流。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces the behavioral level, describing familiar actions such as walking and speaking as largely subconscious. Behavioral design aims to give users a sense of control through usability, understanding, feel, and weight. Examples include a finely made knife, a high-performance car, and a showerhead offering sensory pleasure. A tilting teapot illustrates how changing its position controls tea steeping and separates the leaves from the water. The discussion then connects emotion with safety judgments, action, and communication through bodily movement and facial expressions. The teapot's upright position also signals to a waiter that the tea is ready and may prompt an offer of more water.

points.title: 熟练动作与日常行为的潜意识特征
行为设计的核心：通过可用性与质感建立掌控感
淋浴头带来的感官体验
斜体茶壶通过摆放姿态控制浸泡与茶水分离
情感判断与交流：茶壶姿态向服务员传递状态

chapters.title: 反思性设计：产品如何表达自我形象与价值观
chapters.summary: 反思层面像脑中的旁观者，对事物与行为作出评价。讲者通过悍马车主的自我形象、购买环保汽车的价值表达，以及昂贵手表与功能型电子表的对比，说明产品的意义可以超出其实际功能。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker describes the reflective level, linking it to Freud’s superego and portraying it as an observing inner voice that evaluates things and actions rather than controlling behavior, senses, or muscles. A Hummer owner’s attachment illustrates self-image; buying a General Motors car despite a very high initial price and incomplete warranty illustrates environmental concern. An expensive watch that can be shown off to friends is contrasted with a purely functional digital watch that may keep more accurate time but is described as ugly.

points.title: 反思层面：作为旁观者的内在评价声音
悍马车主：投入情感关乎自我形象
环保汽车：购买选择表达环保价值观
手表对比：炫耀价值与计时功能

chapters.title: 情感的制衡与拟人化家具带来的快乐
chapters.summary: 以游乐设施为例，说明安全感如何制衡对摔倒的恐惧；再以杰克·克拉斯制作的带爪椅子，说明人会接受椅子偷偷捡球的拟人化解释，并从中获得快乐。最后以今后只说事物好话的玩笑收尾。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker explains how one emotion can counterbalance another: reassurance about safety offsets fear of falling, whereas rusty, damaged amusement park equipment would discourage participation. Furniture maker Jack Crass's clawed chair is then described as trying to retrieve a lost ball unnoticed. The audience's willingness to believe this personified explanation illustrates the pleasure emotions can bring. The unit ends with a joke about only saying good things about objects from now on.

points.title: 安全感与恐惧：游乐设施中的情感权衡
带爪椅子捡球：拟人化解释带来的快乐
以“今后只说好话”的玩笑收尾

videos.title: 用统计数据重新认识世界
videos.original_title: The best stats you've ever seen | Hans Rosling
videos.creator: TED

chapters.title: 儿童死亡率测验揭示对世界的先入之见
chapters.summary: 讲者在卡罗林斯卡医学院开设全球健康课程，以五组国家的儿童死亡率比较题测试学生。瑞典优秀学生平均仅答对1.8题，低于随机猜测的预期；教授的表现则与随机猜测相当。讲者借黑猩猩随机选择的比喻，指出问题不只是缺乏知识，更在于先入之见，并强调传播世界发展与儿童健康数据的必要性。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker describes starting a global health course at Karolinska Institute after about twenty years studying hunger with African institutions. A pretest asked Swedish undergraduates to identify the country with higher child mortality in each of five pairs, with a twofold difference within each pair. Students averaged 1.8 correct answers out of five, below the chance performance illustrated by a chimpanzee choosing between two labeled bananas. Karolinska professors performed at chance level. The speaker attributes the students' results to preconceived ideas rather than simple ignorance and stresses the need to communicate data about the world and child health.

points.title: 全球健康课程的背景与课前测验缘起
测验设计：比较五组国家的儿童死亡率
学生成绩：五题平均答对1.8题
黑猩猩比喻：成绩低于随机猜测反映先入之见
教授测试与传播世界健康数据的必要性

chapters.title: 用生育率与预期寿命看世界变化：从两极划分到发展趋近
chapters.summary: 通过国家气泡图展示人口、生育率与出生时预期寿命，检验“西方小家庭、长寿，第三世界大家庭、短寿”的旧印象。动态数据呈现中国、拉美、孟加拉国等地的变化，以及艾滋病对非洲寿命的冲击；再以美国和越南对比，说明亚洲社会变化的幅度容易被低估。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker introduces a country bubble chart in which bubble size represents population and the axes show fertility and life expectancy at birth. He uses changes since 1962 to challenge students' division of the world into a Western world with small families and long lives and a developing world with large families and short lives. The animation discusses China, Latin America, Arab countries, India, Indonesia, Bangladesh's family planning efforts in the 1980s, and the decline in African life expectancy during the HIV epidemic of the 1990s. A comparison of the United States and Vietnam follows Vietnam's gains in life expectancy, declining family size, and transition toward a market economy. The speaker states that Vietnam in 2003 had the same life expectancy and family size as the United States in 1974, emphasizing how easily Asia's social changes are underestimated without examining data.

points.title: 气泡图的读法与“西方／第三世界”的旧印象
生育率、预期寿命与1962年的两类国家
动态观察各国走向更长寿、更小家庭的过程
孟加拉国的家庭计划与非洲的艾滋病冲击
美国与越南对比：数据揭示亚洲社会变化

chapters.title: 全球收入分布：贫富之间的连续谱与亚洲减贫
chapters.summary: 全球收入分布并非贫富两端截然分开，但收入份额高度不均：最富的20%人口占约74%，最穷的20%占约2%，中间人口占24%。各地区收入范围相互重叠，使“发展中国家”的笼统划分受到质疑。回看约1970年至讲述时的变化，亚洲数亿人摆脱贫困；讲者引用世界银行预测，说明人口将更多集中于收入中间段，并指出图表使用对数刻度。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker presents the continuous distribution of global daily income, challenging the idea of a clear gap between rich and poor while highlighting unequal income shares: the richest 20% receive about 74%, the poorest 20% about 2%, and the middle population 24%. Regional distributions for Africa, OECD countries, Latin America, Eastern Europe, East Asia and South Asia overlap, calling the broad category of developing countries into question. Looking back to around 1970 and moving forward, the presentation shows hundreds of millions of Asians leaving poverty while some others enter it. A World Bank projection points toward more people in the middle of the income distribution. The speaker notes the logarithmic scale and relates it to percentage economic growth.

points.title: 全球收入分布连续，贫富之间没有截然断层
收入份额高度不均与“发展中国家”概念的局限
非洲、经合组织国家及其他地区的收入分布重叠
从约1970年看亚洲数亿人摆脱贫困
世界银行预测：更多人口集中于收入中间段

chapters.title: 人均GDP与儿童存活率：地区平均值背后的国家差异
chapters.summary: 以人均GDP和五岁儿童存活率绘制气泡图，气泡大小代表人口，展示收入与儿童健康的强关联。将各地区拆分为国家后，非洲、南亚、阿拉伯国家等内部的巨大差异显现，说明不能用地区平均值概括所有国家。通过贸易、援助及健康表现的例子，强调国家处境各异，且许多差异远大于数据的不确定性。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker replaces family income with GDP per capita and plots regional bubbles against child survival to age five, with bubble size representing population. Regional aggregates show a strong relationship between income and child survival. Splitting regions into countries reveals substantial variation: Sierra Leone, Mauritius and Ghana illustrate differences within sub-Saharan Africa, alongside discussion of trade access and differing needs for aid and investment. Further comparisons include Afghanistan and Sri Lanka, Yemen and the United Arab Emirates, Cambodia and Singapore, Eastern Europe, Latin America and OECD countries. The speaker argues that the observed differences are much larger than the uncertainty in the data and discusses Chile's expected progress relative to Cuba in child mortality.

points.title: 用人均GDP、儿童存活率和人口气泡比较各地区
拆分撒哈拉以南非洲：国家差异与贸易、援助需求
南亚与阿拉伯国家内部也存在巨大差异
国家间的差距远大于数据的不确定性
比较东欧、拉美与OECD国家的健康表现

chapters.title: 各国健康与财富的发展路径：先改善健康的优势
chapters.summary: 通过1960年后各国的变化，说明健康与财富的发展速度并不一致：中国先改善健康，随后增加财富；韩国的进步明显快于巴西，并与乌干达一同作比较。讲者指出，先改善健康似乎更有利于快速发展。阿联酋的例子说明，石油收入不能直接换来健康，还需投资教育、培养医护人员并提高民众教育水平。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker traces countries' development from 1960 onward, describing health gains in China under Mao followed by rising wealth under Deng Xiaoping. A comparison of South Korea, Brazil and Uganda highlights different development speeds, with South Korea advancing much faster than Brazil. The speaker suggests that countries may progress faster when health improves before wealth. The United Arab Emirates illustrates how oil wealth alone cannot buy health: investment in schooling, health staff training and public education is needed. Sheikh Zayed is credited with advancing the country despite falling oil prices, followed by an observation that countries tend to use their money better.

points.title: 中国的发展：先改善健康，随后增加财富
从1960年比较韩国、巴西与乌干达的发展速度
先改善健康似乎更有利于快速发展
阿联酋的石油财富与健康、教育投入
各国趋向更有效地利用财富

chapters.title: 国家平均值掩盖内部差异，改善策略需要细分情境
chapters.summary: 国家平均数据会掩盖国内不同群体的差异。讲者将乌干达、南非和尼日利亚按贫富五等份拆分比较，说明非洲内部情况多样，不能用同一种策略推进不同群体的艾滋病相关普遍可及服务；改善措施需要比区域层面更细致地结合具体情境。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker warns that country averages conceal large differences within countries. Uganda is described as being where South Korea was in 1960, then broken into wealth quintiles to show its internal disparities. South Africa and Nigeria are also examined, including references to the poorest fifth of Nigeria and the richest fifth of South Africa. These comparisons illustrate the diversity of conditions across Africa. The speaker argues that universal access related to HIV cannot use the same strategy for groups at opposite ends of the distribution, and that improvements require detailed, context-specific approaches rather than regional generalizations.

points.title: 国家平均数据可能掩盖国内差异
将乌干达按贫富五等份拆分比较
进一步比较南非和尼日利亚的贫富群体
非洲情况多样，改善策略必须结合具体群体与情境

chapters.title: 让公共统计数据可搜索、可视化：Gapminder的目标与中美收入分布案例
chapters.summary: 公共统计数据虽已存在，却因深藏数据库、收费和密码等障碍而难以利用。讲者介绍Gapminder如何连接数据与设计工具，主张让公共资助的数据免费开放、可搜索，并供人们制作动画。最后以中美收入分布为例，说明1970年两国分布几乎不重叠，此后中国收入增长，同时内部差距扩大。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker explains why existing statistics held by the UN, national statistical agencies, universities and NGOs remain difficult for the public to use, citing inaccessible databases, prices and passwords. He introduces Gapminder as a nonprofit effort to connect data with design tools and animation software, and argues for making publicly funded data freely available and searchable. He describes statistical agencies' resistance and a more encouraging response from the new head of UN statistics. An income-distribution example compares China and the United States in 1970, when their distributions barely overlapped, then shows China's subsequent income growth and increasing inequality, underscoring the value of making this information visible.

points.title: 公共统计数据为何未被有效利用
Gapminder：连接现有数据与设计工具
让数据免费开放、可搜索，突破机构阻力
联合国统计部门的态度与未来展望
中美收入分布：从1970年对比到中国的变化

chapters.title: 结尾：互联网普及、经济水平与公共数据可视化
chapters.summary: 以每千人互联网用户数收尾，介绍软件可访问各国约500项指标，并主张让数据库免费、可搜索，以直观图形帮助生成研究假设。随后对照互联网用户数与人均GDP，指出互联网普及与经济水平密切相关，提及百美元电脑的重要性，以及部分国家互联网增长快于经济的趋势。
chapters.english_summary: In this closing segment, the speaker introduces Internet users per 1,000 people and describes software that provides access to about 500 variables across countries. He advocates making databases free, searchable, and available in readily understandable graphical formats, framing visualization as hypothesis-generating in response to statisticians' concerns. He then compares Internet use with GDP per capita, observes how closely adoption fits countries' economic levels, mentions the importance of the $100 computer, and notes that some countries' Internet adoption is rising faster than their economies, a trend to follow over time.

points.title: 用每千人互联网用户数收尾，介绍各国约500项指标的访问
让数据库免费、可搜索，并转为易理解的图形
回应统计学质疑：可视化用于生成研究假设
对照互联网普及与人均GDP，说明百美元电脑的重要性
观察部分国家互联网增长快于经济的趋势

chapters.title: 片尾宣传：珍视创意与艺术愿景
chapters.summary: 以“伟大的创意若不被珍视会怎样”引出宣传文案，强调保护艺术愿景，让富有灵感的设计构想延续并成为驾驶机器。
chapters.english_summary: The closing promotional passage asks what would happen if great ideas were not cherished or valued, then describes a place where artistic vision is protected and inspired design ideas live on to become ultimate driving machines.

points.title: 设问：创意若不被珍视、失去价值会怎样
保护艺术愿景，让设计构想成为驾驶机器

videos.title: 语言如何塑造我们的思维
videos.original_title: How Language Shapes the Way We Think | Lera Boroditsky | TED
videos.creator: TED

chapters.title: 语言是否塑造思维：从交流能力引出古老问题
chapters.summary: 语言通过声音传递复杂思想，让知识跨越时空传播；“水母在图书馆跳华尔兹并思考量子力学”的想象展示了这种能力。全球约7000种语言在发音、词汇和结构上存在差异，由此引出语言是否塑造思维的问题。演讲以查理曼与朱丽叶的引语呈现不同观点，并预告将用科学研究数据探讨这一争论。
chapters.english_summary: This opening introduces language as a means of transmitting complex thoughts through sound and sharing knowledge across time and space. An imagined jellyfish waltzing in a library while thinking about quantum mechanics illustrates how speech can convey a novel idea. The speaker notes that roughly 7,000 languages differ in sounds, vocabulary, and structure, then asks whether the language we speak shapes how we think. Quotations from Charlemagne and Shakespeare's Juliet frame opposing views in this longstanding debate. The speaker announces that research in her laboratory and others now provides scientific data to address the question, leading into examples.

points.title: 声音如何传递思想与知识
水母的奇异想象：语言传递新想法
语言的差异是否塑造思维？
查理曼与朱丽叶：两种不同观点
从古老争论走向科学研究

chapters.title: 用东南西北说话：语言与文化如何训练方向感
chapters.summary: 澳大利亚 Kuuk Thaayorre 人用东南西北而非左右描述位置，连问候也要报告行进方向。讲者以腿上的蚂蚁、移动杯子和日常问候为例，说明语言与文化如何训练方向感，并让观众闭眼指向东南方，展示不同群体在辨别方向上的差异。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker describes the Kuuk Thaayorre community in Pormpuraaw, Australia, whose language uses cardinal directions instead of left and right. Examples include locating an ant on a leg, asking someone to move a cup, and greeting others by asking where they are going. The speaker argues that language and culture train strong orientation skills, then asks the audience to close their eyes and point southeast. Their varied responses illustrate the contrast with a community where even a five-year-old can identify the direction.

points.title: Kuuk Thaayorre 人用基本方向代替左右
用方向描述蚂蚁、移动杯子和日常问候
语言与文化训练出敏锐的方向感
现场互动：闭眼指向东南方
从观众表现看不同语言群体的方向认知差异

chapters.title: 时间的排列方向：书写习惯与地理方位
chapters.summary: 以祖父不同年龄的照片排序为例，说明英语使用者可能从左向右排列时间，希伯来语或阿拉伯语使用者则可能相反，这与书写方向有关。Kuuk Thaayorre 人无论面朝何方，都按从东到西排列时间，体现了以地理方位而非自身身体为参照的时间观。
chapters.english_summary: Using photographs of her grandfather at different ages, the speaker contrasts ways of arranging time. English speakers may order the photos from left to right, while Hebrew or Arabic speakers may arrange them from right to left, reflecting writing direction. Kuuk Thaayorre people arrange time from east to west: left to right when facing south, right to left when facing north, and far to near when facing east. Their arrangement follows geography rather than the orientation of their bodies, contrasting with the speaker's body-centered way of representing time.

points.title: 祖父照片排序：书写方向与时间排列
Kuuk Thaayorre 人面朝不同方向时如何排序
共同规律：时间始终从东到西排列
以自身为中心与以地理方位为参照的对比

chapters.title: 数字词汇如何帮助精确计数
chapters.summary: 以数企鹅为例，说明计数是让每个对象对应一个数字，并用最后一个数字确定总数的语言技巧。讲者指出，缺少精确数字词汇的语言使用者难以计算精确数量，也难以完成企鹅与同等数量鸭子的匹配任务。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains counting as a linguistic skill through the example of counting penguins: each penguin is assigned a number, and the final number gives the total. The speaker states that some languages lack exact number words such as seven or eight, making precise quantification difficult for their speakers. Matching penguins with an equal number of ducks illustrates how counting supports exact quantity matching and how lacking this linguistic feature limits the task.

points.title: 数企鹅：逐一对应数字，以最后一个数字确定总数
计数是一种从小习得的语言技巧
有些语言缺少精确的数字词汇
用企鹅与鸭子的等量匹配说明计数的作用

chapters.title: 语言的颜色分类如何影响辨色与大脑反应
chapters.summary: 不同语言用不同数量的颜色词划分颜色界限。英语用“蓝色”统称，俄语则区分浅蓝和深蓝。讲者介绍，俄语使用者能更快地区分这两类蓝色；观看浅蓝到深蓝的渐变时，区分两者的人会在类别转换处出现大脑的“惊讶”反应，而英语使用者没有同样反应。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how languages differ in their color vocabulary and category boundaries. English uses one term, blue, whereas Russian distinguishes light blue (goluboy) from dark blue (siniy). The speaker describes tests in which Russian speakers distinguish these categories more quickly, and brain responses to a light-to-dark blue gradient: speakers who name the colors separately show a surprise response at the category transition, while English speakers do not.

points.title: 颜色词的数量与颜色分类界限因语言而异
英语统称蓝色，俄语区分浅蓝与深蓝
辨色测试：俄语使用者更快区分两类蓝色
渐变颜色引发的不同大脑反应

chapters.title: 语法性别如何影响人们对事物的描述
chapters.summary: 本段说明不同语言中的名词语法性别可能影响人们对事物的看法。太阳和月亮在德语与西班牙语中的性别相反；描述桥时，德语使用者更倾向于用“美丽”“优雅”，西班牙语使用者则更倾向于用“强壮”“绵长”。
chapters.english_summary: This unit discusses how grammatical gender can influence perceptions and descriptions of objects. The sun is feminine in German and masculine in Spanish, while the moon has the opposite genders. The speaker states that these differences affect thinking, then uses bridges as an example: German speakers, whose word for bridge is feminine, tend to describe bridges as beautiful or elegant; Spanish speakers, whose word is masculine, tend to use words such as strong or long.

points.title: 不同语言为名词赋予不同的语法性别
太阳与月亮在德语、西班牙语中的性别相反
语法性别是否影响人们的思考方式
桥的语法性别与两种语言使用者的描述差异

chapters.title: 语言如何影响事件记忆、责任判断与认知
chapters.summary: 以意外打碎花瓶和弄伤手臂的表达为例，说明英语与西班牙语等语言如何引导人们关注行为者或意外性质，影响事件记忆、目击证词及责备与惩罚。随后回顾语言对时空排列、数字与数学、颜色感知及名词相关思考的多方面影响。
chapters.english_summary: This unit compares how languages describe accidental events, using a broken vase and an injured arm as examples. It explains that English speakers are more likely to remember who caused an accident, while Spanish speakers are more likely to remember its accidental nature or intent. It discusses implications for eyewitness testimony and shows how describing the same vase-breaking event as 'he broke the vase' rather than 'the vase broke' can increase blame and punishment, even when viewers witnessed the event themselves. The unit then reviews the scope of language's influence through references to time and space, number words as stepping stones to mathematics, color perception, grammatical gender across nouns, and everyday judgments about responsibility.

points.title: 意外事件的表达差异：打碎花瓶与弄伤手臂
语言引导记忆：记住行为者还是意外性质
同一事件的不同措辞如何影响责备与惩罚
回顾语言对时空认知与数学能力的影响
回顾语言对颜色感知、名词思考与日常判断的影响

chapters.title: 结语：珍视语言多样性，反思自己的思维方式
chapters.summary: 语言多样性展现了人类大脑的灵活与创造力，却正在不断消失。演讲者指出，关于大脑和思维的研究过度依赖说美式英语的大学生，限制了我们对人类思维的认识，最后邀请听众反思自己的语言如何影响思考，以及能否创造不同的想法。
chapters.english_summary: The closing section presents linguistic diversity as evidence of the human brain’s ingenuity and flexibility, describing languages as living systems people can reshape. The speaker warns that languages are disappearing, with roughly one lost each week and an estimated half potentially disappearing within a century. She criticizes the narrow reliance on American English-speaking university students in research on the brain and thought, then invites listeners to reflect on how their own language shapes their thinking, whether they could think differently, and what thoughts they want to create.

points.title: 语言多样性体现大脑的灵活与创造力
语言多样性正在消失
思维研究的样本局限与偏见
反思自己的语言如何影响思维
追问能否换种方式思考、创造怎样的想法

videos.title: 压力如何影响记忆
videos.original_title: Does stress affect your memory? - Elizabeth Cox
videos.creator: TED-Ed

chapters.title: 考试时为何突然想不起来：压力与事实记忆的三个环节
chapters.summary: 以考试时想不起“ataraxia”的含义为引子，提出短期压力与事实记忆的关系，并介绍记忆的获取、巩固和提取：新信息激活脑区，海马体在杏仁核影响下巩固记忆，前额叶皮层可能发出提取信号。
chapters.english_summary: An exam scenario in which a student cannot recall the meaning of “ataraxia” introduces the relationship between short-term stress and memory for facts. The unit outlines acquisition, consolidation, and retrieval. Sensory experiences activate brain areas; the hippocampus consolidates memories under the influence of the amygdala, which emphasizes emotionally charged experiences. Encoding probably involves strengthening synaptic connections activated by the original experience. Memories are stored throughout the brain, and the prefrontal cortex likely signals their retrieval.

points.title: 考试中遇到熟悉词语却突然想不起来
关注短期压力对事实记忆的影响
获取：接触新信息并激活相应脑区
巩固与编码：海马体和杏仁核的作用
提取：回忆已编码的记忆

chapters.title: 适度压力如何促进记忆，过度与慢性压力为何有害
chapters.summary: 在记忆的前两个阶段，适度压力可通过皮质类固醇、杏仁核与海马体的作用促进记忆巩固。大鼠实验显示，激素剂量增加时，记忆表现先升后降。人类的适度压力只有与记忆任务相关时才显现益处，如时间压力可能帮助背诵，而朋友的惊吓不会。慢性压力导致激素长期持续作用，可损伤海马体并削弱形成新记忆的能力。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how moderate stress can support the first two stages of memory. Corticosteroids activate threat detection and response in the amygdala, which prompts the hippocampus to consolidate the stressful experience; the hormones also stimulate the hippocampus directly. In rats injected with stress hormones, memory-test performance initially improved as doses increased, then declined at higher doses. In humans, benefits from moderate stress appear only when stress is related to the memory task: time pressure may help with memorizing a list, whereas being scared by a friend does not. Chronic stress can sustain corticosteroid exposure for weeks, months, or years, damaging the hippocampus and reducing the ability to form new memories.

points.title: 适度压力可帮助经历进入记忆
压力激素通过杏仁核与海马体促进记忆巩固
大鼠实验：激素剂量升高，记忆表现先升后降
人类的记忆获益取决于压力是否与任务相关
慢性压力可损伤海马体，削弱新记忆形成

chapters.title: 压力为何让人考试时大脑空白
chapters.summary: 压力会妨碍事实回忆：皮质类固醇刺激杏仁核，进而抑制负责思考、注意和推理的前额叶皮层，使战斗、逃跑或僵住反应在危险时优先发挥作用。这也可能导致考试时大脑空白，而努力回忆本身又会增加压力，形成更难回忆的恶性循环。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how stress impairs the recall of facts. Remembering relies on the prefrontal cortex, which governs thought, attention, and reasoning. Corticosteroids stimulate the amygdala, which inhibits prefrontal cortex activity so that the fight, flight, or freeze response can override slower, reasoned thought in dangerous situations. This can also make the mind go blank during a test. Trying to remember can itself become a stressor, causing further corticosteroid release and making recall even less likely.

points.title: 压力妨碍事实回忆，回忆依赖前额叶皮层
皮质类固醇通过杏仁核抑制前额叶活动
抑制作用让危险应对反应优先于理性思考
考试时大脑空白的可能原因
努力回忆可能加剧压力，形成恶性循环

chapters.title: 应对考试压力：情境练习、运动与深呼吸
chapters.summary: 以考试为例，介绍保持镇定的三种方法：提前在接近真实考试的条件下练习，降低陌生情境引发的压力反应；通过运动缓解焦虑、提升幸福感，并可能改善睡眠；考试当天用深呼吸应对战斗、逃跑或僵住反应，在关键时刻恢复平静。
chapters.english_summary: This unit presents three ways to manage stress, using tests as the main example. Practicing under conditions similar to the test, such as time pressure and sitting at a desk instead of on a couch, can reduce sensitivity to those circumstances. Exercise is linked to brain chemistry changes that reduce anxiety and improve well-being, and regular exercise is widely thought to improve sleep. On test day, deep breathing can counter the fight, flight, or freeze response; studies have shown measurable reductions in test anxiety among groups ranging from third graders to nursing students. The unit closes by recommending a few deep breaths when the mind goes blank and describing ataraxia as a state of calmness free from anxiety.

points.title: 模拟考试条件练习，减少陌生情境带来的压力
通过运动缓解焦虑，并帮助改善睡眠
考试当天用深呼吸减轻焦虑
大脑一片空白时，用几次深呼吸找回平静

videos.title: 睡眠如何帮助学习与记忆
videos.original_title: The benefits of a good night's sleep - Shai Marcu
videos.creator: TED-Ed

chapters.title: 考前熬夜还是睡觉：睡眠对身体与记忆的重要性
chapters.summary: 以凌晨备考和准备钢琴演出的情境引入，指出继续突击学习和练习未必比睡觉更好。睡眠并非浪费时间，而是调节身体重要系统的关键过程；睡眠中的大脑也会进行活跃的重组，这对记忆运作至关重要。
chapters.english_summary: An opening scenario presents a student awake at 4 a.m., facing a test in eight hours followed by a piano recital, and suggests that sleep may be more beneficial than further cramming and practice. The unit challenges the view of sleep as wasted time, describing its role in regulating vital bodily systems, including respiration, circulation, growth, and immune response. It then introduces sleep's importance for the brain, noting blood flow to the brain while falling asleep and active restructuring during sleep that is crucial for memory.

points.title: 凌晨备考与练琴：继续突击还是去睡觉
睡眠不是浪费时间或忙完后的休息
睡眠调节呼吸、循环、生长与免疫反应
睡眠中的大脑重组对记忆至关重要

chapters.title: 从遗忘到长期记忆：海马体与记忆巩固
chapters.summary: 介绍遗忘曲线及将短期记忆转为长期记忆的巩固过程。通过米尔纳对患者H.M.的研究，说明海马体参与事实、概念等陈述性记忆的巩固，并区别于反复练习获得的动作技能记忆。随后说明信息经海马体处理，借助神经可塑性形成新连接、强化神经网络的过程。
chapters.english_summary: Explains Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve, including the loss of 40% of new material within twenty minutes, and introduces memory consolidation as the transfer from short-term to long-term memory. Describes Brenda Milner's research on H.M., whose memory formation was impaired after hippocampal removal while repeated practice still enabled physical learning. Distinguishes declarative memory, such as facts and concepts for a test, from procedural memory, such as finger movements for a recital. Presents a consolidation model informed by Milner and Eric Kandel: sensory information is temporarily recorded in neurons, passes to the hippocampus, and becomes supported by strengthened cortical networks and new synaptic connections through neuroplasticity.

points.title: 遗忘曲线：新材料在最初二十分钟内遗忘40%
记忆巩固：从短期记忆转为长期记忆
H.M.案例：海马体切除后的记忆与动作学习
陈述性与程序性记忆：考试知识和演奏动作
巩固过程：海马体与神经可塑性强化记忆网络

chapters.title: 睡眠如何巩固不同类型的记忆
chapters.summary: 情绪和压力会影响记忆留存，而充足睡眠是记忆巩固的重要因素。非快速眼动慢波睡眠帮助陈述性记忆逐步转入皮层的长期储存，快速眼动睡眠则与程序性记忆巩固有关。讲解以背公式和练音阶后的入睡时间为例，说明减少睡眠会妨碍学习成果的保留。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how heightened emotion, stress, and sleep influence memory retention. It describes electrical activity between brain regions involved in memory formation, then distinguishes non-REM slow-wave sleep, during which declarative memories are repeatedly reactivated and gradually redistributed from the hippocampus to long-term cortical storage, from REM sleep, which is associated with procedural memory consolidation. It cites going to sleep three hours after memorizing formulas and one hour after practicing scales as ideal timing based on the studies discussed, and concludes that insufficient sleep reduces retention of prior learning and practice.

points.title: 情绪、压力与充足睡眠对记忆留存的影响
睡眠阶段与记忆形成相关脑区的电活动
慢波睡眠帮助陈述性记忆转入长期储存
快速眼动睡眠与程序性记忆巩固
背公式、练音阶后的入睡时间与缺觉的影响

videos.title: 不睡觉会对身体和大脑产生什么影响
videos.original_title: What would happen if you didn’t sleep? - Claudia Aguirre
videos.creator: TED-Ed

chapters.title: 连续11天不睡觉：加德纳的经历与睡眠缺失的风险
chapters.summary: 1965年，17岁的兰迪·加德纳连续264小时未睡，先后出现视力无法聚焦、触觉辨物能力丧失、情绪与协调能力变化，以及注意力、短期记忆受损、偏执和幻觉。虽然他恢复后未留下长期身心损伤，但缺觉对其他人可能造成激素失衡、疾病，极端情况下甚至死亡。
chapters.english_summary: In 1965, 17-year-old Randy Gardner stayed awake for 264 hours, or 11 days. The account traces his difficulty focusing his eyes, loss of object recognition by touch, moodiness, poor coordination, concentration and short-term memory problems, paranoia, and hallucinations. Although Gardner recovered without long-term psychological or physical damage, the unit notes that sleep loss can cause hormonal imbalance, illness, and, in extreme cases, death in others.

points.title: 17岁的加德纳连续264小时不睡觉
早期变化：视力聚焦与触觉辨物能力受损
第三天：情绪不稳、动作不协调
实验末期：注意力与记忆困难、偏执和幻觉
恢复情况与缺觉可能带来的严重后果

chapters.title: 睡眠需求、困意来源与非快速眼动睡眠的修复作用
chapters.summary: 睡眠至关重要，成年人每晚需要七至八小时，青少年约需十小时。身体的疲劳信号与环境变暗的信号共同促成困意；腺苷、褪黑素等促眠化学物质增加，使睡眠由浅入深，呼吸和心率减慢、肌肉放松。非快速眼动睡眠期间，DNA得到修复，身体恢复以迎接新一天。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that sleep is essential, although the reasons we sleep are only beginning to be understood. Adults need seven to eight hours per night, while adolescents need about ten. Bodily fatigue signals and environmental darkness contribute to sleepiness. Rising levels of sleep-inducing chemicals, including adenosine and melatonin, lead to progressively deeper sleep, slower breathing and heart rate, and muscle relaxation. During non-REM sleep, DNA is repaired and the body replenishes itself for the next day.

points.title: 睡眠的重要性与不同年龄的睡眠需求
身体疲劳与环境黑暗带来困意
促眠化学物质使睡眠加深，身体逐渐放松
非快速眼动睡眠中的DNA修复与身体恢复

chapters.title: 睡眠不足的身心危害与致死性家族性失眠症
chapters.summary: 本段介绍美国成年人和青少年经常睡眠不足的比例，以及缺觉对学习、记忆、情绪和反应速度的影响，并列举炎症、幻觉、高血压等健康风险。通过球迷熬夜看世界杯后因中风死亡的案例，引出长期短睡眠与中风风险的关联，最后介绍罕见遗传病致死性家族性失眠症及其严重后果。
chapters.english_summary: This unit reports estimates that 30% of adults and 66% of adolescents in the United States are regularly sleep-deprived. It describes effects on learning, memory, mood, and reaction time, along with possible inflammation, hallucinations, and high blood pressure, and links to diabetes and obesity. A soccer fan who died of a stroke after staying awake for 48 hours to watch the 2014 World Cup introduces a reported four-and-a-half-fold increase in stroke risk among people chronically sleeping fewer than six hours nightly compared with those consistently sleeping seven to eight hours. The unit also describes Fatal Familial Insomnia, a rare inherited condition that prevents sleep and progressively leads to dementia and death within months or years.

points.title: 美国成年人和青少年经常睡眠不足的比例
缺觉对认知、情绪与身体健康的影响
球迷熬夜案例与长期短睡眠的中风风险
致死性家族性失眠症：遗传性失眠及其后果

chapters.title: 睡眠如何帮助大脑清除代谢废物
chapters.summary: 科学家认为，大脑代谢废物的积累可能导致睡眠不足的多种负面症状。腺苷积累会增加睡眠压力，咖啡因则阻断其受体通路。睡眠时更活跃的类淋巴系统利用脑脊液清除细胞间的有毒副产物，脑内淋巴管也可能参与废物清理。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the proposed link between sleep deprivation and waste accumulation in the brain. Energy use during waking hours produces byproducts including adenosine, whose buildup increases sleep pressure; caffeine blocks adenosine receptor pathways. Other accumulated waste products are thought to contribute to the negative symptoms of sleep deprivation. The glymphatic system is more active during sleep and uses cerebrospinal fluid to flush toxic byproducts from between cells. Recently discovered lymphatic vessels in the brain may also help clear daily waste. The unit closes by emphasizing that sleep is necessary for health and sanity while its restorative mechanisms remain under investigation.

points.title: 腺苷积累增加睡眠压力，咖啡因阻断其受体通路
其他代谢废物积累可能引发睡眠不足的负面症状
类淋巴系统在睡眠时利用脑脊液清除废物
脑内淋巴管也可能参与废物清理
睡眠对维持身心健康不可或缺

videos.title: 政府为什么不能无限印钱
videos.original_title: Why can’t governments print an unlimited amount of money? - Jonathan Smith
videos.creator: TED-Ed

chapters.title: 央行为何不能靠无限印钞挽救经济
chapters.summary: 以疫情期间美国首轮2.2万亿美元救助引出资金来源问题，说明政府与央行在经济政策和货币供给上的分工。增加货币可能促使企业涨价，而非增产和创造就业，导致购买力下降，即通货膨胀；每年约2%的温和通胀被视为经济健康的信号，过高则可能损害经济。
chapters.english_summary: The unit opens with the economic disruption caused by COVID-19 in March 2020 and the United States' $2.2 trillion first relief package. It distinguishes government policies, such as tax cuts and public infrastructure projects, from central banks' control of the money supply, noting their independence to prevent political interference. It explains why unlimited money creation may fail to support long-term growth: producers of food, clothing, and cars could raise prices instead of increasing production and creating jobs. This reduces purchasing power and is called inflation. Annual inflation of about 2% is described as a sign of economic health, while higher inflation can quickly disrupt an economy.

points.title: 疫情经济冲击与巨额救助的资金来源问题
政府经济政策与央行货币供给管理的分工
无限印钞为何未必促进长期增长
涨价而非增产：通胀如何降低购买力
约2%的温和通胀与过高通胀的风险

chapters.title: 量化宽松：央行购债如何增加资金并促进借贷
chapters.summary: 介绍量化宽松通过央行购买债券创造资金的机制，并解释债券与借债的关系。以美联储在2008—2009年金融危机及2020年的购债为例，说明资金如何支持政府救济，以及大量购债如何降低债券回报，鼓励投资者向企业放贷，进而支持投资、招聘和经济增长。
chapters.english_summary: Explains quantitative easing as central-bank bond purchases intended to inject cash while keeping the risk of severe inflation low. Defines buying bonds as lending money to a corporation or government in return for repayment with interest, and contrasts individuals using existing money with central banks creating money to purchase bonds. Discusses Federal Reserve Treasury purchases during the 2008–2009 financial crisis and in 2020, including the pledge to buy unlimited Treasuries and support for relief such as stimulus checks and unemployment benefits. Explains how large purchases lower bond returns, encouraging investors to lend to riskier businesses and helping firms fund projects and hiring, alongside short-term government relief.

points.title: 量化宽松通过央行购债增加资金流动
购买债券意味着借出资金并获得还本付息承诺
个人购债使用现有资金，央行购债创造新资金
美联储购债及2020年政府救济的案例
购债降低债券回报，推动企业借贷、投资与招聘

chapters.title: 央行购买政府债务的争议与量化宽松的未知后果
chapters.summary: 美联储承诺无限量购买政府债务，引发了政府可能通过发行新债偿还旧债、持续欠央行债务的理论担忧。一些经济学家认为这可能破坏保护经济的制度，另一些则认为这些措施必要且已帮助稳定经济。量化宽松虽日益普遍，但仍较新，其潜在后果仍在展开。
chapters.english_summary: The Federal Reserve’s pledge to buy unlimited government debt raises a theoretical concern: the government could issue new bonds purchased by the central bank and use the proceeds to repay old bonds, effectively never repaying its debt to the central bank. Some economists see such purchases as undermining a system designed to protect the economy; others argue these measures are necessary and have helped stabilize economies. Quantitative easing has become more common but remains relatively new, with potential consequences still unfolding.

points.title: 美联储无限量购买政府债务的承诺引发质疑
理论情景：发行新债偿还旧债，持续欠央行债务
经济学家的分歧：制度隐忧与稳定经济的必要性
量化宽松仍较新，潜在后果尚在展开

videos.title: 经济泡沫是如何形成的
videos.original_title: What causes economic bubbles? - Prateek Singh
videos.creator: TED-Ed

chapters.title: 经济泡沫与荷兰郁金香狂热的兴起
chapters.summary: 以郁金香、房地产和 pets.com 股票说明价格远超价值、持续上涨后骤跌的经济泡沫现象。随后介绍17世纪荷兰的贸易繁荣与富商花园需求，以及郁金香的异域属性、漫长培育周期和病毒造成的稀有花纹如何推动价格与人气上升，催生郁金香狂热。
chapters.english_summary: The unit introduces economic bubbles through tulips, real estate, and pets.com stock: assets sold for far more than they were worth, with prices rising before abruptly falling. It then traces the emergence of Dutch tulip mania, describing Amsterdam's commercial wealth in the 1630s, wealthy merchants' flower gardens, and demand for exotic tulips that could take years to bloom. Tulip breaking virus produced rare, multicolored, flame-like petal streaks, helping drive up prices and popularity until tulips became a nationwide sensation.

points.title: 从郁金香、房产与股票认识经济泡沫
荷兰贸易繁荣与富商的花园需求
郁金香的异域来源与漫长培育周期
病毒花纹的稀缺性推动涨价与郁金香狂热

chapters.title: 投机狂热与泡沫：需求如何推高价格
